details:
Problem
=======
Currently there's no easy way for user's to visit a website for a creator of an avatar, world or any friend's social media posts.
Ideally, user's would want to click a link on a profile or a billboard or display in a world and be able to launch a website.
However, if links were to just open the user's browser are obviously not safe or convenient, especially if the user is in VR and wants to stay in VR.
Solution
========
My idea is while VRChat is open, if you click on a link in a world or in the menu system, it will 'send it to desktop'. This will, if you're in VR, open a small app minimised that will run behind VRC. If you are on desktop, it will open and switch right away.
If you're in VR, when you exit VRChat this app would unminmise and show you the list of URLs you queued up to visit while you were in game. You can choose to open these individually, all at once or remove ones without opening. This would be similar to how Steam Screenshots work and open after you exit a game on that platform so it would be familiar to players.
At any time the user can always access their Desktop (via SteamVR Dashboard or a VR overlay tool) or pop off their HMD and switch to this app by just unminimising it and viewing it, they wouldn't have to quit VRC to do so.
Safety Features
===============
This app could also support a 'report this URL' feature if it turns out a URL they visited is not safe or contains inappropriate content which can let moderators know about it and provide them details for its source in the game.
What kind of URLs you can share could also be moderated on trust level, links in worlds would tie back to their creator's trust level:
New Users: Social Media profile links on their public profile only.
Users: Whitelist of well known and moderated, sites such as YouTube, Wikipedia, News publishers, VRChat forums, etc.
Known: Popular 'indie' shop fronts for performers or avatar/world creators to link to Patreon, Gumroad, Itch.IO, etc.
Trusted: Any URL of any website as long as its not blacklist by VRC or appears on known dangerous site lists (maintained by trusted malware detection services).
